summary.text: WebMCP tools are {webmcp}. Backend, model and connection are set on the Agent page.

loading.text: Reading the settings from the node.

needsConnection.text: The settings live on the node. Set the agent endpoint and the admin token below.

unauthorized.text: The node refused the admin token. Enter it again below.

unavailable.text: This node serves no agent settings. It has no admin principal, or agent settings are switched off.

noBackend.text: {chat} Backend: not chosen. Choose a backend to start.

sessionExpired.text: The settings did not load because your sign-in has ended.

stepUp.text: Changing agent settings needs a recent second-factor sign-in. Use the button under Connection.

notEligible.text: This account may not read or change agent settings. Ask the person who runs this node to add you as an admin.

step2.title: Connect it.
step2.text: Enter the URL and type its host to confirm it, test the connection, then apply. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint also needs a model.

step3.title: Turn on agent chat.
step3.text: Use the switch under Features. The chat button appears once it is on.

url.label: Base URL
url.help: https, or http on this machine. Example: http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1

error.empty: Enter the URL of the backend.
error.invalid: This is not a valid URL.
error.scheme: Use https, or http on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1].
error.extras: Remove the username, password, query and fragment.

key.label: API key
key.help: Optional. Write-only: the node keeps it in a private file in its settings directory and never shows it again. Test connection and chats use the stored key, so save a new key before you test. The node sends it only to the backend host it is stored for; moving the backend to another host needs a new key.
key.helpServer: Optional. Write-only: the node keeps it in a private file in its settings directory and never shows it again. Test connection and chats use the stored key, so save a new key before you test. A key this node reads from the server follows a host change; a key stored through this page does not.

source.settings_api: Written by this page. It is never shown again.
source.environment: Read from an environment variable on the node. It is never shown.
source.file: Read from a file on the node. It is never shown.

saved.text: The node holds it now. Test the connection to use it.

cleared.text: The node no longer holds a key.

serverManaged.text: Set on the server (Kubernetes Secret). This node does not accept keys through the settings page. Test connection and chats use the key the server holds.

removeConfirm.label: Confirm removing the key
removeConfirm.text: Remove the stored key? Tests and chats then send no key.

key.withApply: The key is sent with Apply, together with the URL and the host you confirm. It is not saved before then.
key.helpWithApply: Optional. Write-only: the node keeps it in a file only it can read and never shows it again. The key goes with Apply, so a test before Apply may answer that a key is needed. The node sends it only to the backend host it is applied for.

test.note: The test asks the node to reach the URL.

ok.models: {count, plural, one {# model listed.} other {# models listed.}}
ok.noModels: The endpoint hides its model list. Type a model name.
ok.noModelsKeyWithheld: The model list needs the stored key, and it was not sent to this host. Type a model name.

failed.text: The node could not reach this endpoint.

test.gated: Test connection stays off until you type the host {host} above. A test of a new host never carries the stored key, and the key does not follow a move: supply a new key with the change.
test.gatedServer: Test connection stays off until you type the host {host} above. A test of a new host never carries the stored key. After you apply, the key the server supplies goes to the new host.

keyNotSent.text: Only the current backend receives the stored key, and this host is not it. The key does not follow a move to this host: supply a new key with the change. An endpoint that needs a key may still refuse you.

test.keyNotSentServer: This test did not send the key. Before you apply, a test of a new host never carries the key; after you apply, the key the server supplies goes to this host. An endpoint that needs a key may still refuse you.
test.noteNewHost: The test asks the node to reach the URL. A test of a new host never carries the stored key, and the key does not follow a move: supply a new key with the change.
test.noteNewHostServer: The test asks the node to reach the URL. A test of a new host never carries the stored key. After you apply, the key the server supplies goes to the new host.

model.label: Model
model.help: Pick from the list or type a model name the endpoint accepts.
model.disabled: Test the connection to load the model list. This field stays off until the endpoint has answered.
model.count: {count, plural, one {# model available} other {# models available}}
model.noMatch: No match. Press Enter to use what you typed.

url.label: Instance URL
url.help: The address of your Universal Agent Runtime instance. https, or http on this machine. This node has no default.

test.note: The test asks the node to reach the instance.
test.noKey: The test reads the instance's public agent card and sends no API key.

failed.text: The node could not use the Universal Agent Runtime instance at {host}.

agent.label: IPFS agent
agent.text: The node keeps the API key in a file only it can read and sends it only to this instance, to create and run the agent.

uar.applyFailed: The node could not set up the runtime. Check the instance URL and the API key, then test the connection.

key.help: Write-only: the node keeps it in a file only it can read and never shows it again. The node sends it only to this instance, when it creates and runs the agent. Test connection sends no key.
key.helpServer: Write-only: the node keeps it in a file only it can read and never shows it again. A key this node reads from the server is sent to this instance when the agent is created and run. Test connection sends no key.

saved.text: The node holds it now and sends it to this instance on the next run.

removeConfirm.text: Remove the stored key? The node then sends no key to the instance.

serverManaged.text: Set on the server (Kubernetes Secret). This node does not accept keys through the settings page. The node sends the key the server holds to this instance.

confirmServerManaged.text: A key this node reads from the server (an environment variable or a file) follows a host change: after you apply, the node sends it to the new instance. Check the host before you apply. To use a different key there, change it on the server.

confirm.help: Node content an agent reads, any API key you enter with this change, and this node's MCP grant (when one is configured) go to this host. Apply stays off until you type the host exactly.

confirm.label: Type the backend host to confirm:
confirm.help: Node content that an agent reads goes to this host. Apply stays off until you type it exactly.

matches.text: Apply can send node content to {host}.

confirm.differs: Not the same yet. Type the host exactly as shown.
confirm.helpKey: The key stored through this page does not follow to a new host: applying removes it. To use a key there, choose Replace key and type it before you apply.
confirm.helpKeyServer: A key this node reads from the server is sent to the new host too.

serverManaged.text: A key this node reads from the server (an environment variable or a file) follows a host change: after you apply, chats and Test connection send it to the new host. Check the host before you apply. To use a different key there, change it on the server.

applying.text: Sending the settings to the node. You can keep reading the form.

applied.text: At {time}. New chats use {model} at {host}. A chat in progress finishes on the previous backend.
applied.textUar: At {time}. New chats use the IPFS agent on Universal Agent Runtime at {host}. A chat in progress finishes on the previous backend.

failed.text: Nothing was changed. The previous backend is still in use.
failed.textFirst: Nothing was changed. No backend is set yet.

elsewhere.text: The node's settings changed from another tab or client. Your edits are kept. Reload to see the current values before you apply.

dirty.text: Apply sends the backend settings to the node. A chat in progress finishes on the backend it started with.

blocked.confirm: Type the host above to confirm the change.

firstRun.text: Choose a backend and fill in its settings, then apply. The chat answers only after that.

clean.text: These are the settings in effect.

conflict.text: The node's settings changed while you were editing. They were reloaded and your edits are kept. Retry to apply your edits on top, or Reload settings to take the node's values.

keyNotCarried.text: The key for the old host is not sent to the new host.
keyNotCarried.prompt: Replace key and type a new key if the new host needs one.

failure.generic: The change did not go through.
failure.unauthorized: The node refused the admin token. Sign in again.
failure.route_absent: This node serves no agent settings.
failure.network: Cannot reach the node. Check that ipfs mcp is running and that this page may connect to it.
failure.protocol: The node answered with something that is not settings.
failure.unavailable: The settings service did not answer as expected.
failure.revision_conflict: The settings changed while you were editing. They were reloaded; check the values, then try again.
failure.egress_confirmation_required: The node needs the new model host confirmed. Type {host} above.
failure.secrets_not_accepted: This node does not accept keys through the settings page.
failure.step_up_required: Agent settings need a recent sign-in with a second factor. Use the button under Connection, then retry.
failure.forbidden: This account may not change agent settings.

features.title: Features
features.lede: Each switch applies as soon as you flip it and is kept in this browser. None of them is part of the backend that Apply sends.

chat.title: Agent chat
chat.help: Shows the chat button. While off, the page loads nothing and sends no request.

needs.text: The switch is on, but no valid /agui address is set, so the button stays hidden. Set one under Connection.

confirm.title: Desktop confirmation window
confirm.help: Asks you in a separate IPFS Desktop window before an agent change runs.
confirm.tray: Switch this in the IPFS Desktop tray menu. This page cannot change it.

policy.subject: Writes and deletes
policy.note: Writes and deletes ask you first. This cannot be turned off here.

connection.title: Connection
connection.lede: The settings route lives on the same node as the chat endpoint. This page reads and writes it with an admin token that is separate from the chat token.

managed.text: The local agent service is managed by IPFS Desktop.

stopped.text: The local agent service is not running. IPFS Desktop starts it when the agent is on.

managed.help: The endpoint and the keys are held by the Desktop app. There is nothing to enter here.

admin.label: Admin token
admin.help: The bearer token of the admin principal of ipfs mcp. It can change the model backend. It is held in memory, tied to the agent endpoint above (a different endpoint forgets it) and sent only as an Authorization header to that node.
admin.heldMemory: A token is held in memory for {root}. Reloading this page forgets it.
admin.heldTab: A token is kept for this tab, for {root}. Closing the tab forgets it.

refused.text: The node refused the admin token. Enter it again.

keep.label: Keep for this tab
keep.help: Keeps the token in this tab's session storage so a reload does not ask again. Session storage is shared by every page this site serves, including any content it shows, so keep it only where you trust all of that. It is never written to local storage.

noRoot.text: Set a valid agent endpoint first. The admin token is tied to it and sent nowhere else.
